title: pipeFile streams file to response with no error handler — read error crashes the runner
note: Verified. pipeFile (lines 80-87 of the current file) does `createReadStream(path).pipe(res)` with NO `.on("error")` listener and no `res.on("close")` cleanup — grep for stream.on/res.on/headersSent/.destroy in the file returns nothing. The error mechanism is sound: pipeFile returns void synchronously after registering .pipe(), so streamIMessageAttachment's promise resolves before any stream 'error' fires; asyncRoute's `void handler(...).catch(next)` (index.ts:530) therefore cannot intercept the async stream error. An unlistened ReadStream 'error' becomes an uncaught exception. Crucially, the process-level handler at index.ts:4154 `process.on("uncaughtException")` logs and then calls `process.exit(1)` (line 4168) — so a read failure mid-stream (file unlinked/permission-revoked between statSync at line 81 and the read; Messages.app attachment cleanup; OS upgrade) deliberately kills the entire Express+Playwright runner, downing all platforms. This is strongly corroborated by commit d03a4a1/5d425f3 ('fix(runner/imessage): ... attachment-server stream errors ...') which added exactly this `stream.on('error')` + `res.on('close')` guard — but that commit is NOT an ancestor of the current HEAD (git merge-base --is-ancestor returns false), so the fix is absent on this branch. Critical severity stands.
suggestedFix: Port the guard from the never-merged commit d03a4a1: register `stream.on('error', err => { if (!res.headersSent) res.status(500).json({error:'stream read failed'}); else try { res.destroy(err); } catch {} })` and `res.on('close', () => { if (!stream.destroyed) stream.destroy(); })` BEFORE calling stream.pipe(res), so a mid-stream read failure or client disconnect can no longer reach process.on('uncaughtException')->process.exit(1).

title: Dedupe merges distinct humans by displayName label alone, cross-contaminating threads and deleting Person rows
note: Verified. main() selects only id/displayName/createdAt/notes (line 21 — NOT handle) and groups purely on p.displayName.trim().toLowerCase() (line 26). For every group of 2+ it re-parents all duplicates' threads onto the canonical (lines 41-44) and prisma.person.delete()s the duplicate (line 54) with no identity check. The adapter (platforms/imessage-adapter.ts resolveDisplayName, lines 59-68) produces non-unique displayNames: 1:1 chats fall back to the raw chatIdentifier when the vcf misses (line 62), and groups comma-join per-participant handles with raw fallback (lines 65-67). Person.handle exists in the schema (line 85) but is never compared. So two genuinely distinct identities that share a label — two unresolved phone strings, two real contacts both named e.g. 'John Smith', two different groups with the same unresolved participant set — get merged: identity B's threads move under A and B's row is destroyed. Irreversible cross-contamination + record loss on the exact path the script walks. Severity critical is correct.
suggestedFix: Match on a stable identity, not the displayName label. Persist/compare Person.handle (already in schema, line 85) and merge only rows whose normalized handle/phone matches (the resolver exposes siblingHandles(handle) at contact-resolver.ts:155 for grouping multiple numbers of one real contact). Skip any group whose key is empty/blank or still phone-shaped (an unresolved handle is not proof of same-human), and default to a dry-run behind an explicit --apply flag.

title: Scheduling a send silently drops staged composer attachments
note: Re-verified independently. scheduleSend (lines 1180-1205) posts ONLY { text, clientSendId, scheduledFor } via JSON apiPost at 1188-1192 — it never reads or appends composerAttachments. The immediate onSend path (929-991) by contrast detects attachmentsToSend.length > 0 and uploads them via FormData (947-959), proving the multipart capability exists and is only wired into the immediate path. The schedule-send button gate at line 3519 is `disabled={!composer.trim() || sending || scheduling}` with no reference to composerAttachments, and the preset/custom buttons (3536, 3556) gate only on `scheduling`. On success scheduleSend clears setComposer("") (1193) but never clears composerAttachments, so the chips rendered at 3625-3651 linger with empty text. iMessage attachments are real (file input gated on thread.platform === 'IMESSAGE' at 3577). Net effect: operator stages photos/files + text, schedules, the later-fired message carries text but no attachments, with zero warning — genuine silent content loss. High severity is justified (irreversible loss of user-attached content on a path the operator believes succeeded).
suggestedFix: Prefer (b): in scheduleSend, when composerAttachments.length > 0 build a FormData (mirroring onSend at 947-959) including each a.file and the scheduledFor field, then clear composerAttachments and revoke preview URLs on success. If the scheduled-send runner endpoint cannot yet persist attachments, instead (a) disable the schedule button when composerAttachments.length > 0 with a tooltip, and surface a toast/inline note that scheduled sends can't carry attachments — never drop them silently.

title: Menu actions (Reconnect / Run selector tests / Reset session) use runAction — no pending state, silent on success
note: Verified. The cited line range 262-299 is stale (the file is 290 lines), but the described code genuinely exists: Reconnect (lines 182-187), Run selector tests (lines 193-198), and Reset session… (lines 211-215) all call runAction(...), NOT runActionWithFeedback. runAction's success branch (lib/api.ts:69-74) only does setError(null) — no toast, no pending UI. The Menu closes immediately on select (menu.tsx:60-62: setOpen(false) before item.onSelect()), so there is no surviving control to flip and zero success signal. The two sibling actions on the same menu — 'Scan now' (line 167) and 'Open browser/Connect' (line 144) — correctly use runActionWithFeedback, which fires a 60s pending toast then a success/error toast via the ToastHost mounted in components/layout/app-shell.tsx:197. The runner endpoints are genuinely slow: /control/platform/reset-session (index.ts:3951) acquires a global reset lock, aborts the scan queue, and awaits every platform mutex before wiping the profile dir; /control/platform/test-selectors (index.ts:1378) drives a real selector-test service under a platform control lock; /control/platform/connect (index.ts:1214) runs a connect op. The only failure signal is the shared actionError string at the top of the page. This directly violates the product's stated bar.
suggestedFix: Route all three onSelect handlers through runActionWithFeedback like 'Scan now' directly above. Reconnect: { pending: `Reconnecting ${PLATFORM_DISPLAY[row.platform]}…`, success: `${PLATFORM_DISPLAY[row.platform]} reconnected`, failure: `Couldn't reconnect ${PLATFORM_DISPLAY[row.platform]}`, setError: setActionError, onDone: () => refresh() }; mirror for Run selector tests and the destructive Reset session (which most needs a pending toast given the global reset lock).

title: Name confirm/rename/dismiss has no error feedback and leaks an unhandled rejection on failure
note: Confirmed. call() (lines 59-69) awaits apiPost inside try/finally with NO catch. apiPost (apps/dashboard/lib/api.ts:96-115) throws ApiRequestError on any non-ok response, and the underlying fetch rejects when the runner is offline — so the await genuinely rejects on failure. On rejection: the finally runs setBusy(false) (clearing the disabled state), the success branch (setOpen(false)/setEditing(false)/onChanged()) is skipped so the popover stays open unchanged, and the rejection propagates out of the async fn. Every caller invokes it as `void call({...})` (lines 111, 125, 147), making it an unhandled promise rejection. The component imports only apiPost (no @/lib/feedback, no showToast), holds no error state, and has no catch anywhere — so there is zero user-visible error signal. An established pattern exists and is used elsewhere: runActionWithFeedback + showToast in apps/dashboard/lib/feedback.ts, rendered via toast-host.tsx (mounted in app-shell.tsx) and used in apps/dashboard/app/platforms/page.tsx:144,167. (The description's top-status.tsx:460 citation did not resolve to a matching line, but the platforms/page.tsx precedent is real, so the finding holds.) This violates the product's 'every action must surface a success or error signal' bar.
suggestedFix: Route the call through runActionWithFeedback(apiPost(`/runner/control/person/${personId}/rename`, body), { pending: 'Updating name…', success: 'Name updated', failure: "Couldn't update name", onDone: () => { setOpen(false); setEditing(false); onChanged(); } }) so pending→success/error toasts fire and the popover only closes on success. At absolute minimum, add a .catch in call() that surfaces showToast({ kind: 'error', ... }) (or sets an inline error) and keeps the popover open, so the rejection never floats as an unhandled rejection.

title: Send verification falsely reports success via timestamp_advanced when no message bubble was actually sent
lines: 9203-9211, 9286-9304 (finding cited 9847-9868; code has since shifted, file is 9367 lines)
note: Verified against the real code, which lives at different line numbers than cited but matches the evidence exactly. getLatestMessageSnapshot (l.9199-9213): reads the last bubble's <time>, tries the datetime attr (l.9200) then innerText (l.9201), Date.parse()s it (l.9203), and on NaN substitutes Date.now() (l.9211). I confirmed Date.parse("4:52 PM")/"19:16"/"10:59 PM" all return NaN in Node, and the file's own comments (l.6118-6120: 'almost always just the time of day... LinkedIn drops [datetime] on most prod renders') establish the NaN->Date.now() path is the COMMON case. In the verify loop (l.9286-9307) the ONLY signals are the LAST bubble's direction + timestamp (+ optional textMatch); there is NO message-count or stable-key delta check (grepped the loop, none). timestampAdvanced = !preSend || last.timestamp > preSend.timestamp (l.9293) is therefore essentially always true from read-time clock drift when both snapshots synthesize Date.now(). When the most recent visible bubble is already OUT (operator re-replying where they sent last) and the new send silently fails to post, last.direction==="OUT" && timestampAdvanced (l.9301) fires and returns verifiedBy='timestamp_advanced'. Downstream send.ts treats ANY returned receipt as success: it upserts the OUT message (l.297-320), sets thread.lastOutboundAt/lastMessageText/unreadCount:0 (l.330-346), sets SendRequest.status='SENT' (l.348-354), and emits MESSAGE_SENT (l.368-374) with no inspection of verifiedBy. So a silently-failed LinkedIn send is recorded and surfaced as sent. The robust bubble_detected branch (l.9296, gated on textMatch) is fine; the defect is specifically the timestamp_advanced fallback combined with synthesized timestamps. High severity holds for the re-reply scenario.
suggestedFix: Disable the timestamp_advanced path when the timestamp was synthesized. Have getLatestMessageSnapshot return a flag (e.g. timestampSynthetic: Number.isNaN(parsed)) and, when true, require textMatch (bubble_detected) rather than accepting timestamp_advanced. Better: capture the OUT message-bubble COUNT and/or the last bubble's stable platformMessageKey (data-event-urn) pre-send and only accept success when the count increases or a NEW OUT bubble whose text matches appears. As-is, on unparseable timestamps the timestamp_advanced branch (l.9301) must not be allowed to confirm a send.

title: Beta send returns a success receipt even when the send-button click failed and Enter was a no-op (silent send failure)
note: Verified. In sendMessage the send-button click is `page.locator(selectors.send_button).first().click({ timeout: 10000 }).catch(async () => { await page.keyboard.press("Enter"); })` (lines 402-404) followed by an unconditional `return { sentAt: ..., verifiedBy: "best_effort" }` (406-409) — no post-send verification of any kind. send.ts confirms the downstream consequence: parseReceipt/dispatch (lines 277-374) takes ANY returned receipt, upserts the OUT message row, updates the thread (lastMessageText, lastMessageAt, lastMessageDirection=OUT), sets sendRequest.status="SENT", and emits MESSAGE_SENT — all independent of receipt.verifiedBy, so "best_effort" is treated as fully terminal exactly like "bubble_detected". By contrast the LinkedIn adapter sendMessage (linkedin-adapter.ts:9280) does a bare `.click({ timeout: 10_000 })` that throws on failure (no .catch), then runs a real 10s verify loop (9286-9307) polling getLatestMessageSnapshot for an OUT bubble with advanced timestamp and matching text before returning. The beta path neither verifies nor lets a click failure surface, so if the selector has drifted (click times out) AND Enter doesn't dispatch on the IG/TikTok composer surface (newline / not focused), the user is told the reply was sent when it never left the browser. Note: the finding's cited line range (428-436) is off — the actual code is at 402-409 — but the described code and behavior unambiguously exist.
suggestedFix: Mirror the LinkedIn adapter: capture a pre-send snapshot, do not swallow the send-button click (or if Enter fallback is used, still verify), then poll the conversation for a new OUT bubble whose text matches and/or an advanced last-message timestamp. Only return a receipt when verification passes; otherwise throw an AdapterFailure (kind THREAD_FETCH_FAILED/SELECTOR_MISMATCH) so send.ts records FAILED and the dashboard shows an error + retry instead of a false success.

title: cancelScheduledSend reads-then-writes without a status guard — can mark an already-sent message CANCELLED
lines: 540-560 (finding cites 582-598, which is actually updateScheduledSend's doc/signature; the cancel logic is at 540-560)
note: Verified real. cancelScheduledSend (lines 540-560) does `await prisma.sendRequest.findUnique` (yields the event loop), checks `row.status === 'SCHEDULED'`, then issues an UNCONDITIONAL `prisma.sendRequest.update` keyed only on clientSendId setting status:CANCELLED. The route handler at index.ts:1682 calls it with no mutex/transaction. The scheduled-send promoter (scheduled-send-promoter.ts) runs on its own independent setInterval (started at index.ts:237) and is NOT serialized against this handler; its tick() flips SCHEDULED→PENDING via updateMany then calls sendQueue.kick(). In the single Node process the promoter's timer callback can dispatch during the cancel handler's awaited findUnique, promote the row, and the queue worker can drive processSendRequest to the adapter. processSendRequest reads status exactly once (send.ts:226-229) and never re-checks before/after the adapter call, so a late CANCELLED write does NOT stop the in-flight send. Result: the message is actually delivered but the SendRequest row terminal-states as CANCELLED and the operator is told 'cancelled'. Corrupted terminal state + false success signal on a real outbound message justifies high. (DB is SQLite, no transaction wrapping; confirmed via packages/core/prisma/schema.prisma.) Note the finding's line range is off by ~40 lines but the described code unambiguously exists.
suggestedFix: Make the cancel atomic and conditional: replace the unconditional update at send.ts:557-560 with `const r = await prisma.sendRequest.updateMany({ where: { clientSendId: input.clientSendId, status: 'SCHEDULED' }, data: { status: 'CANCELLED' } })` and treat `r.count === 0` as losing the race (`return { cancelled: false, reason: 'no_longer_scheduled' }`). The SQL-level WHERE status='SCHEDULED' makes the check-and-set a single statement, closing the promoter interleave.

title: runOnce() drives the shared LinkedIn page without the enrich lock, racing a concurrent background drain on the same Playwright page
note: Verified. processJob acquires the enrich lock around the profile visit (enrichment-queue.ts:294 tryAcquire(deps.enrichLockKey, () => visitProfile(...))). runOnce calls visitProfile(personId) directly at line 371 with no enrich-lock acquisition; its only guard (lines 361-364) checks operationMutex.isRunning for scan/send keys, NOT the enrich key. session-manager getManagedPage returns the cached per-platform Page (session-manager.ts:123-134 reuses state.pages.get(platform)), so processJob's in-flight extractProfile and a runOnce fired by the manual-refresh ?wait=1 endpoint (index.ts:3302) drive the SAME Chrome page concurrently. One call's page.goto can interrupt the other's DOM extraction ('Execution context was destroyed') or cross-contaminate the profile persisted via persistSuccess. The lock key is a single fixed constant (default:LINKEDIN:ENRICH, index.ts:173-175), so this is a true unguarded shared-resource race.
suggestedFix: Acquire the enrich lock in runOnce just like processJob: const acquired = await deps.operationMutex.tryAcquire(deps.enrichLockKey, () => visitProfile(personId)); if (!acquired.acquired) return { deferred: true }; const result = acquired.value; then proceed with the existing success/failure branches.

title: Duplicate Person notes are silently lost when the canonical row already has notes
note: Verified. Line 46 copies the duplicate's notes onto the canonical only `if (!canonical.notes && dup.notes)`. When the canonical already carries notes, that branch is skipped and the duplicate is deleted at line 54 with no merge, append, log, or warning — any operator-written notes on the duplicate are permanently discarded. The 'avoid clobbering' comment describes protecting the canonical, but the net effect on the non-canonical row is silent data loss. Severity high is supportable (operator-authored content, irreversible), though it is bounded by how often both rows carry notes.
suggestedFix: When both canonical and duplicate have non-empty notes, concatenate the duplicate's notes onto the canonical with a separator (e.g. a dated divider) instead of dropping them; at minimum log a loud warning that prints the duplicate id and its notes before deleting so the operator can recover them.

title: Unrecognized --platform silently falls back to wiping LINKEDIN
note: Verified against the code. options.platform is initialized to "LINKEDIN" (line 16). In parseCliArgs the --platform branch (lines 21-28) only reassigns options.platform when the uppercased value EXACTLY equals LINKEDIN/INSTAGRAM/TIKTOK/IMESSAGE; on any other value (typo, abbreviation like 'insta'/'ig', misspelling like 'LINKDIN') the if is false, the index is still advanced, and the loop continues with the LINKEDIN default intact. There is no 'unrecognized platform' branch or abort. run() (lines 44-66) then calls resetPlatformInboxGraph(options.platform) which I confirmed in admin-reset.ts (lines 99-172) deletes ALL sendRequests, drafts, messages and threads for that platform plus orphaned Person rows. validateAdminResetGuards (admin-reset.ts lines 73-97) only checks the env token and that confirm==='RESET' — it never validates the platform. So an operator who fat-fingers --platform while supplying a valid token and RESET silently wipes the entire LinkedIn graph instead of the intended platform. The canned npm script db:reset:linkedin hardcodes '--platform LINKEDIN', so this fail-open only bites a manual/direct invocation, and it requires a valid ADMIN_RESET_TOKEN + RESET — but within those (expected operator) conditions the wrong-target, irreversible deletion is real and silent. High retained: silent irreversible mass-delete of the most-populated platform.
suggestedFix: Track whether --platform was supplied and validate its value: if --platform is present but not one of the four valid platforms, throw/exit non-zero with an explicit 'Unrecognized platform: <value>' message instead of silently keeping the LINKEDIN default. Ideally make --platform required (no implicit default) for a destructive wipe so a missing/typo'd flag aborts rather than defaulting to LinkedIn.

title: Bulk-action result (success and error) renders at the top of the page while the action bar is pinned to the bottom of the viewport
note:
Accurate against the real code (note the cited line 663-665 is actually 456-458 in this file version, but the described element matches exactly). bulkResult renders as a plain

in normal document flow at lines 456-457, directly under the error line and just below the sticky PageHead/filters/KPI tiles — it is NOT inside any sticky/fixed container. The bulk action bar is `fixed bottom-6 left-1/2` (lines 510-512) and unmounts the moment runBulk calls clearSelection() (line 342), which empties selectedIds and flips selectMode false. There is no scrollIntoView/scrollTo/focus anywhere in the file to bring the result into view. While the buttons do show in-flight labels ("Marking…"/"Snoozing…"/"Rescanning…", lines 525/535/545), that pending feedback disappears with the bar on completion, so the sole completion signal — especially the partial-failure summary at line 337 ('Mark done: 3 ok, 2 failed (…)') — lands at the top of the page, off-screen on any long inbox where the user just clicked a bottom-pinned button. No toast/TopStatus exists on this page (grep confirms). Real feedback-placement gap; medium because the action still completes and in-flight state was shown, but the result (notably partial failures) can be missed.
suggestedFix: Surface the bulk completion result where the user's attention is rather than at the top of the document — render it inside/just above the fixed bulk bar before clearSelection() dismisses it, or emit it as a toast. Keep the partial-failure string ('N ok, M failed') prominent since that is the case most likely to be missed.

title: "Open in {platform}" kebab action shows no pending or success feedback
note: Re-verified. Line 2620-2621: `runAction(apiPost('/runner/control/thread/${thread.id}/open', {}), setError)` — passes only setError, no onDone. runAction (apps/dashboard/lib/api.ts:58-81) on success merely calls setError(null) (no toast, no ticker) and on failure writes the inline error slot; it never shows a pending state. The Menu component (components/ui/menu.tsx:60-63) calls setOpen(false) then item.onSelect(), so the menu closes instantly and provides no in-flight UI of its own. The /open endpoint drives a Playwright browser focus/open that can take seconds. Result: no pending indicator, no success confirmation — only a possible error. This genuinely violates the product's every-action-surfaces-feedback bar. Medium is appropriate (no data loss; degraded feedback on a slow action). Note: the finding's suggestedFix claim that runActionWithFeedback is 'already used in this file' is inaccurate — it is imported (line 23) but never called anywhere in this file; every runAction call here (e.g. Reassess at 2343, Rescan at 2627) is the plain no-feedback variant. The gap is real regardless.
suggestedFix: Switch to runActionWithFeedback(apiPost('/runner/control/thread/${thread.id}/open', {}), { pending: `Opening in ${platformLabel}…`, success: `Opened in ${platformLabel}`, setError }). The helper (lib/feedback.ts:66-104) emits a pending toast that it replaces with a success/error toast — giving the required in-flight + outcome signals.

title: "Remind me…" shows no in-flight feedback during the AI parse
note: Re-verified. onSelect (2569-2616) calls window.prompt, then immediately apiPost('/runner/control/thread/${thread.id}/remind', { intent }) which is an LLM natural-language time parse. Both terminal outcomes ARE handled: a success toast (2591-2595) and two error paths (2598-2605 for needsClarification/failure, 2608-2614 for thrown errors). However there is NO pending toast, ticker update, or disabled/spinner before or during the apiPost — the Menu closes instantly (menu.tsx:60-63) and nothing signals work is happening until the round-trip returns. So for a multi-second action the operator sees the prompt close then a silent gap, which contradicts the product bar requiring a running state. Medium is correct: less severe than the 'Open' gap because terminal feedback does eventually arrive (the operator is never permanently uncertain), but the in-flight signal is genuinely absent. Confirmed pending toast kind is supported (lib/feedback.ts:7) so the fix is viable.
suggestedFix: Before the apiPost, capture a pending toast id and showToast({ id, kind: 'pending', title: 'Setting reminder…' }), then in .then replace it with the success toast (reuse the id) and in .catch replace it with the error toast — or refactor to runActionWithFeedback (already imported) so pending/success/error are handled uniformly.

title: Background poll overwrites in-progress note draft (keystroke loss)
note: Confirmed but narrower than described. The 10s setInterval (line 86) calls loadList()->setPeople, and `selected` is derived from people (lines 108-111). The effect at 116-123 keys on [selectedId, selected?.notes] and unconditionally runs setNotesDraft(selected?.notes ?? '') + clears notesSaveTimer, with no dirty/focus/saving guard. savedNotesAtRef.current is written at line 151 but grep confirms it is never read, so the intended 'recently edited, don't clobber' guard genuinely does not exist. However, a routine poll where server notes are unchanged does NOT clobber: selected?.notes keeps the same primitive value, so React's Object.is dependency check skips the effect. The real loss window is post-save typing: after the 600ms debounce POSTs and calls loadList (line 156), `selected.notes` updates to the just-saved (older) value while the user has typed further; that value differs from the prior render's, so the effect re-fires, overwrites notesDraft with the stale saved text, and clears the pending timer for the newer keystrokes — silently dropping them. So the mechanism is real, just triggered by the save->refresh cycle rather than 'every poll'.
suggestedFix: Reset the draft only on selectedId change. In the [selectedId, selected?.notes] effect, skip setNotesDraft when notesStatus === 'saving' or when the field is dirty/focused (or when Date.now() - savedNotesAtRef.current is within a grace window). Reconcile server notes into the textarea only when it is not actively being edited.

title: loadDetail swallows fetch errors and wipes the open profile to null with no feedback
note: Confirmed. loadDetail (62-70) does apiGet(...).catch(() => null) then setDetail(data), so any fetch failure replaces detail with null. apiGet (lib/api.ts) only throws ApiRequestError — there is no global toast or event surfacing, so the swallowed error reaches the user nowhere. fetchStarters (235-239) calls loadDetail(selectedId, true) and only toggles startersLoading; on failure the entire enriched panel collapses — the render gates ProfileSections on `detail` (392-396), starters on detail?.starters (398-414), and the summary falls back to 'Not enriched yet' (364-371) — so About/mutuals/openers/id-card all vanish back to the empty state with no message. The initial detail load (line 98) has the same silent-null behaviour. Downgraded from high to medium: nothing is destroyed server-side and the panel self-heals on the next successful fetch, but a user-triggered 'Start a conversation' action visibly wiping the profile with zero feedback is a genuine error-handling + UX-bar gap.
suggestedFix: In loadDetail, catch into setError (or a toast) and do not overwrite a populated detail with null on failure — keep the previous detail. For fetchStarters specifically, fetch/merge only the starters into the existing detail object rather than replacing the whole response, so a failed openers fetch can never blank an already-enriched profile.

title: Focus-mode 'mark handled' advances before archive resolves; error lands on the wrong thread
note: Confirmed. runAction (lib/api.ts line 58) is declared `): void` — it attaches .then/.catch internally and returns undefined, never the promise. So `await runAction(apiPost(...archive), setFocusError, refresh)` in handleMarkHandled (206-214) awaits undefined and resolves on the next microtask while the archive POST is still in flight, then advance() runs immediately (setFocusError(null) + setFocusIndex(i => i+1)). If the archive later rejects, runAction's .catch fires setFocusError(message) — but focusIndex has already moved on, so the message is shown against a different thread's card, and the failed thread (not optimistically removed in this path — optimistic removal only exists in the batch runBatch flow, lines 233-251) reappears after refresh. The three modal buttons (skip/mark handled/open thread, lines 459-463) have no disabled prop, so the in-flight archive shows no spinner and double-clicks are unguarded. Downgraded high->medium: real mis-attribution and missing pending state, but recoverable and limited to the focus-mode modal.
suggestedFix: Await the actual apiPost in a try/catch (don't rely on runAction's void return); only advance() on success, and on failure keep the current thread with focusError attributed to it. Add a `handling` pending flag to disable skip/mark-handled/open-thread while the archive is in flight, giving visible feedback and preventing double-submit.

title: DegradedBanner 'Run selector tests' / 'Run tests' fire with no pending or success feedback
note: Verified. The cited lines 98-106 are stale; the actual handler is at page.tsx:82-88, where onRunSelectorTests is wired to runAction(apiPost('/runner/control/platform/test-selectors', ...), setActionError, refresh). degraded-banner.tsx renders both the inline 'Run selector tests' link (lines 42-49) and the 'Run tests' Button (lines 91-95) with no disabled/pending prop and no busy state. runAction is silent on success (only setError(null)), and the underlying selector test (index.ts:1378) is a real browser-driven operation under a control lock, so the operator gets no spinner, no 'running', and no confirmation — only a refresh. On failure the sole signal is the shared actionError line at the very top of the page, detached from the banner. Genuinely no user-visible signal fires for this action.
suggestedFix: Switch the onRunSelectorTests handler on page.tsx:82-88 to runActionWithFeedback (pending: `Running ${PLATFORM_DISPLAY[row.platform]} selector tests…`, success: `${PLATFORM_DISPLAY[row.platform]} selector tests done`, failure: `${PLATFORM_DISPLAY[row.platform]} selector tests failed`, setError: setActionError, onDone: () => refresh()), so the degraded-state remediation surfaces a pending toast and a clear result.

title: Platforms/logs initial load swallows fetch errors and renders an empty/idle UI with no error signal
note: Verified. The cited lines 47-54 are slightly off; the actual code is at page.tsx:39-46. refresh() does Promise.all([apiGet('/runner/data/platforms').catch(() => []), apiGet('/runner/data/logs?limit=150').catch(() => [])]) then setRows(platforms ?? []) / setLogs(logRows ?? []). On any transport failure both resolve to [], and the UI renders the same empty state ('No platforms reported by the runner.' at line 265-267, no degraded banners) as a genuine zero-platform state. There is no load-error flag and no manual retry — refresh only runs on mount (useEffect line 48-53) and on the 'runner-resync' event. A runner-down failure is indistinguishable from a healthy empty inbox, so the operator sees a falsely-healthy screen. Note: unlike a pure data list, the runner is normally expected to report platforms, so an empty result is itself suspicious — but the swallow still hides the distinction.
suggestedFix: Track a load-error state distinct from empty data: set an error flag inside each .catch (e.g. setLoadError(true)) and render a 'Couldn't reach the runner — Retry' affordance (button calling refresh()) instead of the empty 'No platforms reported' state when the fetch actually failed.

title: Activity log fetch failure is swallowed and shown as 'Nothing logged yet.'
note: Verified. The cited lines 141-146 are stale (the file is 142 lines); the actual code is at logs/page.tsx:38-43 — refresh() does apiGet('/runner/data/logs?limit=300').catch(() => [] as AuditLogRow[]) then setLogs(rows). title: Demo start buttons fire an async runner POST with no pending/disabled/success feedback
note: Verified against commit 57594f5 (the session's HEAD; the shared main tree had been reverted to an older commit by a concurrent session, which is why the path 404'd initially). Confirmed the real start triggers: the Sandbox card onClick={() => void start("sandbox")} (line 71) and the "Start live demo" Button onClick={() => void start("live", selected)} (line 51). start() (FullDemoProvider.tsx 267-303) awaits apiPost("/runner/control/settings") then awaits refreshSettings() — a real network window. During that window NO user-visible signal fires: the buttons have no disabled attr, no spinner, no label change, no pending toast, and no TopStatus update. The only success signal is setFlow("presenter") flipping `active`, which mounts the overlay only AFTER the awaits resolve (local setState is synchronous post-await), so nothing renders during the in-flight window. Error path DOES toast (lines 279-285), so only in-flight + success feedback is absent, exactly as the finding states. This violates the product's stated bar and the memory note. The fix is well-supported: lib/feedback.ts already exports a "pending" ToastKind (spinner, replaced by success/error via reused id) and a runActionWithFeedback() helper doing precisely pending→success/error; the sibling reconnect/page.tsx (RefreshState machine, disabled while running, "Scoring…" label) does it correctly. Minor inaccuracy in the finding's prose (it calls the live-mode card a start trigger; line 88 actually only does setPickingLive(true)) — does not affect the verdict since the two cited start triggers are correct.
suggestedFix: In FullDemoStartScreen, track an in-flight state (e.g. const [starting, setStarting] = useState<null|"sandbox"|"live">(null)) set before start() and cleared in a finally; disable the Sandbox <button>, the "Start live demo" <Button>, and show a spinner/label while starting. Or simplest: wrap the apiPost in start() with the existing runActionWithFeedback({ pending: "Starting demo…", success: "Demo ready", ... }) so the in-flight→success/error toast fires for free.

title: "Open profile" gives no success feedback for a remote browser action
note: Verified. openProfileInRunner (lines 42-54) only ever sets opening/openError state; the try block's success path does nothing on resolve. The button (lines 85-96) shows 'opening…' while in flight and renders openError inline, but on success the label simply reverts to 'open profile ↗' with zero confirmation. The effect lands in the OFF-SCREEN runner-controlled Chrome (comment lines 37-41 confirm this), so the operator gets no signal that the request succeeded vs silently no-op'd. The runner route (apps/runner/src/index.ts:1797-1837) returns a concrete { status: 'ok' } on success, so a success result IS available to surface. The codebase already establishes the norm for exactly this kind of off-screen-Chrome action: the platforms page 'Open browser' button (apps/dashboard/app/platforms/page.tsx:144-152) wraps the analogous open-browser call in runActionWithFeedback with success toast '<Platform> opened'. Keep the existing inline openError or drop it in favour of the toast's error branch.

title: Skipping the tour while the sandbox is still seeding orphans the demo sandbox (real inbox stays hidden, no teardown)
note: Independently verified across PilotTour.tsx, FullDemoProvider.tsx, demo-threads.ts, today/page.tsx and api.ts. The bootstrapping branch of skipTour (PilotTour.tsx 78-85) deliberately omits fullDemo.exit() (the comment even says so). startTour's POST is fullDemo.startPilotSandbox(), which awaits an apiPost that has no AbortController (api.ts 83-94), so a Skip during the in-flight window cannot cancel it. When the POST resolves, FullDemoProvider.startPilotSandbox runs setFlow('pilot')/setMode('sandbox') unconditionally (FullDemoProvider 328-329) — there is no 'was-skipped' guard. That makes sandboxActive true (line 399: flow==='pilot'), and Today/Inbox filter rows to demo-only via scopeRowsToSandbox (demo-threads.ts 24-25; today/page.tsx 277), hiding the operator's real threads. recoveryNeeded is flow===null && presenterFlagsOn (line 394), so with flow==='pilot' it stays false — no recovery banner. Critically, there is genuinely no visible exit: PilotTour returns null once state.active is false (line 170), and FullDemoBanner returns null because showActive=active&&mode where active=(flow==='presenter') is false for the pilot flow, and recoveryNeeded is false too (FullDemoBanner 18-19); its 'Exit demo' button is gated on presenter-active, not on flow!==null. It self-heals only on reload: startPilotSandbox never calls writeFullDemoState, so flow hydrates to null on reload, then refreshSettings reads the persisted presenterDemoMode='sandbox' and trips recoveryNeeded. All load-bearing claims hold. Severity kept at medium: the trigger is a narrow timing race (clicking Skip during the seed POST) and the state is recoverable via reload or Settings, but the consequence — real inbox masked across Today/Inbox with no in-app exit for the session — is real and user-visible.
suggestedFix: In skipTour's bootstrapping branch, don't leave the sandbox half-engaged. Set an abortedRef=true (and still mark seen / clear active / hide the card), then have startTour check abortedRef right after `await fullDemo.startPilotSandbox()` and call `await fullDemo.exit()` instead of clearing bootstrapping — exit() is reentrant via endingRef and tears down the seed. Alternatively, await the in-flight start, then run the normal endTour(true). As a defense-in-depth backstop, also widen FullDemoBanner so its exit affordance shows for any non-null flow (or when recoveryNeeded), not just presenter-active, so an orphaned pilot sandbox still surfaces an Exit button without a reload.

title: Command-palette scan actions fire silently with no pending/success/error feedback
lines: 50-57 (the finding cites 61-81, which is wrong — that block is the thread-item map + onKeyDown; the actual scan action is the "Run scan now" item at lines 50-57)
note: The underlying gap is real. The palette imports only apiGet/apiPost (line 5), never lib/feedback. The single 'Run scan now' item (lines 50-57) runs `void apiPost("/runner/control/scan", {}).catch(() => undefined)` and the click/Enter handlers then call onClose() (lines 90, 119). No showToast, no runActionWithFeedback, no disabled/pending state, no ticker push fires off the click itself. HOWEVER several specifics in the finding are inaccurate and were NOT verified: there is only ONE scan entry, not two — no 'Full LinkedIn rescan' item, no `scope:"update"`/`scope:"full"` payloads exist anywhere in the dashboard (grep-confirmed, same on main); and there is no `TopStatus.onScanNow` and no top-status.tsx — the component is system-status-bar.tsx and has no scan-now button at all (only a cancel/abort button). Severity lowered to medium: the success case does eventually surface via the status bar, and this is one non-destructive palette entry.
suggestedFix: Route the single 'Run scan now' palette item (command-palette.tsx lines 50-57) through runActionWithFeedback (lib/feedback.ts), mirroring app/platforms/page.tsx:167: runActionWithFeedback(apiPost('/runner/control/scan', {}), { pending: 'Checking for new replies…', success: 'Scan started', failure: "Couldn't start scan" }). Inspect the resolved body for the ScanControlBlockedResponse shape (types.ts:181) to show an honest 'just scanned / already running' message on reason 'cooldown_active'|'in_flight'.

title: Scan failures and `ok:false` rejections from the palette are swallowed (silent no-op)
lines: 55 (the finding cites 65-67 and 78-80, which is wrong — the swallowing happens on the single scan line 55; there is no second scan action at 78-80)
note: Confirmed as a more precise statement of the same one line. command-palette.tsx:55 is `void apiPost("/runner/control/scan", {}).catch(() => undefined)`: the .catch swallows network/HTTP errors, and because there is no .then the resolved body is discarded. The discarded body genuinely can be a blocked result — types.ts:181-188 defines ScanControlBlockedResponse { ok:false, blocked:true, reason:'cooldown_active'|'in_flight', retryAfterSeconds }. So on a throttled/in-flight scan or an unreachable runner, runnerStatus never newly becomes SCANNING, the status bar never flips, and no error/info toast appears — the command silently does nothing. Real and user-visible. And 'TopStatus.onScanNow handles all of these explicitly' is false — no such handler exists; the correct comparison is app/platforms/page.tsx:167. The cited 78-80 second action does not exist.
