title: Saving an analysed reply-style suggestion discards the operator's edits even when the save fails
note: Confirmed. saveReview (L219-228) does `await persist(review); setReview(null);` inside a try whose only cleanup is setSavingReview(false). persist (L119-130) swallows its error (L127-129) and never throws, so setReview(null) executes on failure too. Once review is null, the style fields fall back to profile values (styleText, L166-167) and, because persist's catch never updates profile on failure, they revert to the last-persisted values — the AI suggestion plus any manual edits the operator typed into the review buffer (a non-auto-saving buffer, per L93-95) are gone. The only failure signal is the header label flipping to 'failed to save' (L248); the reviewed/edited text is not recoverable from the UI. Severity adjusted to medium: the AI-suggested portion is regenerable by re-running Analyse, but manual edits are lost, and the loss is silent within the pane.
suggestedFix: Make persist report success (return boolean or throw). In saveReview, only call setReview(null) when the save succeeded; on failure keep `review` intact and surface an inline error inside the review pane so the operator's edits survive and can be retried.

title: Start-demo buttons fire a network seed with no pending/disabled state (and allow double-seed)
note: Confirmed. The sandbox card (L68-83, onClick `void start("sandbox")`) and the live button (L48-54, onClick `void start("live", selected)`, disabled ONLY when selected.length===0) both invoke start() which awaits apiPost('/runner/control/settings') + refreshSettings (FullDemoProvider L267-303). FullDemoStartScreen has no `starting`/pending state (only useState for pickingLive and selected), so during the in-flight round-trip neither button disables or shows a spinner — no pending feedback. On error start() shows an error toast and returns (FullDemoProvider L278-285); on SUCCESS there is no toast/ticker — the only signal is the FullDemoOverlay mounting once `active` flips, and `setFlow("presenter")` happens only AFTER the await (L287), so the start screen stays mounted and clickable throughout the network call. start() has no re-entry guard (unlike runAnalyze's `if (analyzing) return` and unlike startPilotSandbox's `flow==="presenter"` guard), and apiPost (lib/api.ts L83) is a plain fetch with no dedupe — so a double-click re-POSTs settings and re-seeds. Severity medium: the success outcome is eventually well-signaled by the overlay, but the in-flight pending state and double-submit guard are genuinely absent.
suggestedFix: Add a local `starting` boolean set before calling start(); disable both option buttons and show a Starting…/spinner state while it runs, and add an in-flight guard at the top of FullDemoProvider.start (early-return if a start is already pending) so a double-click cannot POST settings / seed the sandbox twice.

title: Live-demo thread selection is never enforced — all real threads stay visible despite the explicit privacy promise
note: Confirmed. The copy promises selection scopes visibility: LiveThreadPicker L13-18 ('no auto-include, so private conversations are never surfaced just because they happen to be in the inbox') and FullDemoStartScreen L10-16 ('can never accidentally surface every private conversation in the inbox at once'). selected is passed to start('live', selected) (L50-54), but FullDemoProvider.start only stores it: setLiveThreadIds + writeFullDemoState({...liveThreadIds}) (L291-298). A full grep of liveThreadIds across the branch shows ONLY storage (provider state/context value L81,129,148,297,413,435 and full-demo-state.ts serialization + tests) — nothing consumes it to filter rows. Inbox/Today visibility is gated by sandboxActive (today L270 + inbox L255, via scopeRowsToSandbox), and sandboxActive = `flow==="pilot" || (flow==="presenter" && mode==="sandbox")` (FullDemoProvider L399) is FALSE in live mode. scopeRowsToSandbox (lib/demo-threads.ts L20-25) returns `rows` unchanged when !sandboxActive, so every real thread renders during a live presenter demo. The selection is cosmetic. Correctly scoped as a visibility/privacy gap, not a write risk: the live fetch interceptor (FullDemoProvider L166-185) still blocks mutations. Severity medium — broken privacy guarantee, but read-only and operator-present.
suggestedFix: Enforce the selection: thread liveThreadIds into the inbox/Today scoping (e.g. when flow==='presenter' && mode==='live', filter visible rows to the selected ids — either client-side alongside scopeRowsToSandbox or by sending the ids to the runner). If enforcement is out of scope, remove the copy in LiveThreadPicker (L13-18) and FullDemoStartScreen (L10-16) that promises private conversations won't be surfaced, so the UI stops claiming a guarantee the code does not keep.

title: apiGet discards the runner's error body, surfacing only "Request failed: <status>"
note: Verified in lib/api.ts: apiGet (lines 37-39) throws `new Error("Request failed: " + response.status)` without ever reading the body, whereas apiPost (lines 96-115) calls parseErrorPayload and throws a typed ApiRequestError with the error/message/reason fallback chain. The asymmetry and the lost runner error body are exactly as described, and the thrown value for GETs is a plain Error (no .status/.payload). Impact is real: multiple live callers surface the message verbatim to the operator — people/page.tsx:56-57 (commented as the '#74 explicit error surfacing' pattern), archived/page.tsx:31, and at-risk/page.tsx:121-122 all do setError(err.message), so a 4xx/5xx GET with an explanatory body shows the opaque 'Request failed: 500' instead. NOTE: the finding's specific citations are partly inaccurate — there is no apps/dashboard/app/reconnect/page.tsx file, and settings/page.tsx has no writeCadence/preview error path (only restartRunner's health-poll, which swallows via .catch(()=>false)). The cited proof callers are wrong but the underlying defect and consequence are genuine via the callers above. Most other apiGet callers swallow errors with .catch(()=>null/[]), so this is a message-quality gap, not a crash — medium is appropriate.
suggestedFix: Mirror apiPost in apiGet: on !response.ok, call parseErrorPayload(response), derive the message from the error/message/reason/rawText chain (falling back to `Request failed: ${status}`), and throw new ApiRequestError(message, response.status, payload, rawText). Factor the shared body-to-message logic out of apiPost so both paths stay in sync.

title: Snooze does not actually hide or de-risk the thread (snooze is a silent no-op)
note: The durable mechanism is exactly as described and verified. POST /control/thread/:threadId/snooze (index.ts:3933-3939) writes ONLY slaDueAt + riskReason; it does not touch riskLevel, needsReply, or archivedAt. grep for 'snoozedUntil' returns zero matches across the whole repo + schema — no snooze column exists. loadVisibleThreadRows (index.ts:613-616) filters solely on archivedAt; services/thread-row-shaping.ts toInboxRow (196-228) returns source.riskLevel unchanged and needsReply via deriveNeedsReply (130-135), which is computed purely from lastInbound/lastOutbound timestamps. The next scan (services/scan-queue.ts:2782-2789) and the next send (services/send.ts:330-336) both overwrite riskLevel/slaDueAt/riskReason/needsReply from calculateRisk, and calculateRisk (packages/core/src/risk.ts:52) derives slaDueAt = lastInboundAt + amberMs — so even the cosmetic SLA countdown is wiped. The endpoint returns {status:'ok'} for an action that persists nothing durable. ONE OVERSTATEMENT: the dashboard's Today/Inbox/At-Risk pages each optimistically add the id to a removedIds Set (today/page.tsx:105-121, inbox/page.tsx:306-310, at-risk/page.tsx) and their refetch reconciliation keeps it removed while the server still reports needsReply!==false (today/page.tsx:61-70) — and since snooze leaves needsReply truthy, the row stays hidden for the rest of the live session. So it is NOT visible 'the only visible change is the SLA text' during the acting session; it reappears only on a full page reload or in any other client/view. The bug is real (non-durable snooze, wiped by scan/send, no controlling field) but the immediate-UX consequence is softer than stated, hence medium not high.
suggestedFix: Add a durable snooze field (e.g. snoozedUntil DateTime? on Thread) set by the snooze route, and filter it in loadVisibleThreadRows (OR: [{ snoozedUntil: null }, { snoozedUntil: { lte: now } }]). Make calculateRisk/scan/send respect an active snooze instead of recomputing slaDueAt from lastInboundAt, so the snooze survives reloads, other views, and the next scan.

title: AI provider clients have no request timeout; user-visible calls can hang for up to 10 minutes per attempt
note: Core mechanism verified. The three OpenAI-SDK clients are constructed at ai.ts:691-697 (not 1228-1236) with `new OpenAI({ apiKey })` / `+ baseURL` and NO `timeout` or `maxRetries`. providerOptions (ai.ts:460-463) returns only GPT-5 reasoning overrides / {}, and geminiExtraBody (478-491) only sets thinking config — so no per-request timeout is passed on any of the ~10 chat.completions.create call sites (e.g. 751, 1074, 1217, 1434). withTimeout (index.ts:503) is used solely at index.ts:1277 for the CONNECT flow, never around an AI call; the only AI-side setTimeout (ai.ts:856) is the backoff sleep. config.ts timeouts (CONNECT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS) are browser-only. tryProvider (ai.ts:749-789) does layer an app-level retry loop (maxAttempts: GLM 3 / Gemini 3 / OpenAI 2) on top of any SDK-internal retries, multiplying latency before fallback. So an unbounded hang on a wedged connection is genuinely possible and the dashboard pending state (e.g. 'Drafting…' / 'Reassessing') would just spin. HOWEVER the finding's headline supporting claim is fabricated: ai-providers.ts:200-206 does NOT reason about 'the whole 30s client timeout' — those lines are Gemini 429/5xx error classification, and a repo-wide search finds no '30s'/'30_000'/'client timeout' reasoning anywhere. No real-world hang is evidenced. Downgrading high→medium: real latent risk, but speculative impact and a key cited justification does not exist.
suggestedFix: Set an explicit bound when constructing each client, e.g. `new OpenAI({ apiKey, baseURL, timeout: 30_000, maxRetries: 0 })`, letting the app-level tryProvider loop own retries; make the value configurable via runnerConfig. Do not justify it by an ai-providers.ts comment about a 30s timeout — no such comment exists.

title: applyVoiceRules replaces every colon with a comma, corrupting times/ratios/URLs in generated reply text
note: Verified. applyVoiceRules (ai.ts:541-549) runs `.replace(/:/g, ",")` unconditionally (and `.replace(/;/g, ".")`). It is applied to operator-sendable text in generateSuggestedReplies (ai.ts:1056), transformReply (ai.ts:1087), generateContactSummary (ai.ts:1232) and composeInVoice (ai.ts:1449). So 'let\'s do 6:30' -> '6,30', 'the score was 2:1' -> '2,1', and 'https://x' -> 'https,//x'. The model is told to avoid colons but routinely emits clock times in casual replies, and this is content the operator can send verbatim, so the corruption can reach the recipient. The cited line range (945-954) is wrong but the described code is real. Medium is appropriate — meaning-changing on a minority of outputs, not a crash.
suggestedFix: Scope the colon replacement to prose punctuation only: replace `:` with `,` just when preceded by a letter and followed by whitespace (e.g. /([A-Za-z])\s*:\s+/ -> '$1, '), leaving `\d:\d` (times/ratios) and `://` (URLs) intact. Same care for the semicolon rule near URLs.

title: A generation that fails citation-validation caches an empty starter set under the live cache key, permanently blanking starters
note: Verified. getOrGenerateStarters builds `result = { starters: validated, ..., validatedCount: validated.length }` and persists it via prisma.personEnrichment.update with the current cacheKey unconditionally (lines 203-212), even when validated.length === 0. The cache-hit branch (181-183) does `const cached = safeJsonParse<...>(row.startersJson, null); if (cached) return cached;` — and safeJsonParse (61-68) returns the parsed object, so an empty `{ starters: [], validatedCount: 0 }` is truthy and is returned without regenerating. The only server caller is index.ts:3173-3174 (gated on req.query.includeStarters === '1', not line 4736), and the dashboard 'Start a conversation' button calls fetchStarters -> loadDetail(selectedId, true) -> GET /person/:id?includeStarters=1 (people/page.tsx:235-238, 62-66) with no force/bypass param. There is no force-refresh endpoint anywhere. So one bad model run (cited fields that happen to be empty in the enrichment payload) blanks starters until the contact's enrichment snapshot changes enough to alter stableHash. The inline comment 'the operator can click Refresh to re-roll' (line 192) does not hold.
suggestedFix: When validated.length === 0, return the empty result WITHOUT persisting it (so the next read regenerates), or skip the cache write when it would overwrite an existing non-empty set. Better: add a real force-refresh flag (e.g. ?refreshStarters=1) that bypasses the cacheKey, and wire the 'Start a conversation'/Refresh button to send it.

title: updateScheduledSend rewrites the row without a status guard — can desync a row the promoter just promoted
lines: 600-618 (finding cites 638-657, which is actually the return block; the read+write logic is at 600-618)
note: Verified real, same TOCTOU shape as cancel. updateScheduledSend reads via `await findUnique` (line 600, yields), checks `row.status === 'SCHEDULED'` (line 605), then issues an UNCONDITIONAL `prisma.sendRequest.update` on clientSendId writing requestText/scheduledFor (lines 616-618). Route handler index.ts:1649 wraps it in no mutex/transaction. The promoter's independent interval can flip the row SCHEDULED→PENDING between the read and the write; the worker by then has already copied requestText into its local `input` (send.ts:258) so the OLD text is what actually goes out, while this update overwrites requestText (and possibly moves scheduledFor) on a row that is now PENDING/SENT. The stored row no longer reflects what was delivered. Lower impact than the cancel race (no false 'cancelled' claim, the message still sends), so medium not high — it is a stored-record desync, not a mis-delivery or lied-to-outcome. Finding's cited line range is off but the code is present and matches the description.
suggestedFix: Guard the write on status the same way: `const r = await prisma.sendRequest.updateMany({ where: { clientSendId: input.clientSendId, status: 'SCHEDULED' }, data: { requestText: nextText, scheduledFor: nextScheduledFor } })` and `if (r.count === 0) return { updated: false, reason: 'no_longer_scheduled' }`, so an edit that lost the race to the promoter is reported (409) rather than silently corrupting a promoted/sent row.

title: A throwing subscriber aborts emit() mid-loop, dropping the event for all other subscribers and propagating into the emitter (e.g. send loop)
note: Verified. emit() (event-bus.ts:28-30) iterates subscribers in a for...of with no per-listener try/catch. The live SSE listener (index.ts:901-903) calls writeEvent -> res.write() (index.ts:880-885), neither of which is guarded. A res.write on a destroyed/half-closed socket throws (ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED/EPIPE), which aborts the for...of (later subscribers miss the event) and unwinds into emit()'s caller. emit() is genuinely called from critical paths: send-queue.ts:103 fires SEND_QUEUE_UPDATED inside tick(), whose try has only a finally (resets running) and no catch, so the throw escapes tick() to the process-global unhandledRejection net. Severity lowered to medium because index.ts:909 req.on('close') calls unsubscribe(), so a cleanly-closed client is removed; the exposure is the narrow window where the socket is unwritable before 'close' fires or under write backpressure — real but not constant.
suggestedFix: Wrap each listener call in its own try/catch in emit() so one failing subscriber cannot stop delivery to the others or propagate into the emitter: for (const listener of subscribers) { try { listener(event); } catch (err) { console.warn('event listener threw', err); } }. Optionally auto-unsubscribe a listener that throws.

title: seedDemoData creates 15 persons/threads/messages + an audit log without a transaction; a mid-seed failure orphans records the manifest never captures
note: Verified. seedDemoData (demo.ts:33-92) runs ~15 independent prisma.person.create / thread.create / message.createMany calls plus a final auditLog.create (103-114) with no $transaction. The caller persists the manifest only after full resolution (index.ts:1107 setDemoSeedManifest(manifest)). A mid-loop throw commits the records created so far but never saves the manifest; cleanupDemoData is entirely manifest-driven (demo.ts:127-155 deletes by manifest.threadIds/personIds/logIds), so on leaving demo mode there are no IDs to delete and the partial demo threads stay permanently in the real inbox. The fixed platformThreadId `demo-${platform}-${i}` collides with the schema's @@unique([platform, platformThreadId]) (schema.prisma:263), so an orphaned prior run makes the very next seed throw mid-loop, compounding the orphans. Pre-seed cleanup at index.ts:1095-1101 only helps when a manifest exists, which is exactly what a partial failure lacks.
suggestedFix: Wrap the whole seed in prisma.$transaction so a partial failure rolls back, or build/persist the manifest incrementally inside a try/catch that runs cleanup of the partial IDs before rethrowing.

title: getSettings JSON.parse of stored settings has no try/catch — a corrupt app_settings row throws and breaks every settings read
note: Verified. getSettings parses record.valueJson with an unguarded JSON.parse (settings.ts:63), spread over defaultSettings. getSelectorOverrides (104) and getDemoSeedManifest (162) are likewise unguarded, while getOperatorProfile (181-189) defends with try/catch — confirming the inconsistency. A truncated/corrupt app_settings row makes JSON.parse throw and rejects getSettings with no fallback to defaultSettings. getSettings is read on many control routes (index.ts:1037,1050,1090,1847,2738,3595) and at boot (start() at index.ts:4174 awaits settingsStore.getSettings()), so one bad row turns into a process-wide/startup failure.
suggestedFix: Wrap the parse in try/catch and fall back to defaultSettings (mirroring getOperatorProfile): let parsed: Partial<AppSettings> = {}; try { parsed = JSON.parse(record.valueJson); } catch { parsed = {}; } const loaded = { ...defaultSettings, ...parsed };. Apply the same guard to getSelectorOverrides and getDemoSeedManifest.

title: Concurrent thread cascade-delete and explicit child deletes make returned counts non-deterministic
note: Verified against the actual code. schema.prisma uses provider "sqlite" (line 6) with no relationMode override and no previewFeatures, Prisma 6.3.1 (package.json:32). Thread's children SendRequest/Draft/Message all declare `thread Thread @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade)` at lines 352/300/286, so deleting threads removes the child rows. In admin-reset.ts lines 110-137 the four deleteMany calls (sendRequest, draft, message, thread) fire concurrently inside one Promise.all with no ordering and no $transaction (grep confirms $transaction appears nowhere in the file). Because SQLite serializes the writes in non-deterministic order, if `thread.deleteMany` (and its cascade) runs before `message.deleteMany`, the explicit child delete finds rows already gone and returns count 0 while the cascade actually removed them. Those counts are surfaced straight to the user: res.json spread at index.ts:714-718, and into the audit log at index.ts:700-705. The data outcome itself is still correct (every child row is deleted by either the explicit delete or the cascade, and orphan-people cleanup runs after), so this is a feedback/accuracy + minor atomicity defect, not data loss — hence medium, not higher.
suggestedFix: Run the deletes inside client.$transaction sequentially in child-to-parent order (sendRequest, draft, message, then thread) so each returned count reflects rows that statement actually deleted. Simplest correct option: delete only threads and rely on the declared Cascade, then derive child counts up front via count() before deleting if the response/audit numbers are needed — rather than racing redundant explicit deletes against the cascade.

title: Content-Disposition built from sender filename can throw ERR_INVALID_CHAR for non-Latin1 / emoji / CRLF names
note: Confirmed, with scope corrected. Line 85 builds Content-Disposition from downloadName sanitised only by `.replace(/"/g, "")`. downloadName is `transferName ?? <fallback>` (lines 62/72/77); transferName is the RAW chat.db `transfer_name` column (imessage-db.ts:264 `transfer_name AS transferName`, returned unsanitised at line 281) passed via index.ts:1027. I empirically tested Node v20.20.0 (engine target >=20.0.0) with exactly `name.replace(/"/g,"")`: an emoji filename ('photo<emoji>.jpg') THROWS ERR_INVALID_CHAR, and a CRLF name THROWS ERR_INVALID_CHAR. So the throw on emoji/CJK/non-Latin1 sender filenames is real. This throw occurs synchronously inside streamIMessageAttachment before the pipe, so asyncRoute catches it and returns a bare 500 — the attachment silently fails to render in the dashboard with no explanation (a real UX failure on legitimate international input), NOT a crash (contrast finding 1). Two corrections to the finding: (1) plain Latin1 accented names (cafe-u with diacritics) do NOT throw — only chars OUTSIDE Latin1 (emoji, CJK, Arabic, etc.) do, so 'non-ASCII ... very common' is too broad; the accurate trigger is 'outside Latin1'. (2) Node rejects bare CR/LF by THROWING, so it is not an exploitable header-injection vector under current Node, just another throw path. The hardcoded fallbacks are safe. Corroborated by commit d03a4a1 ('Content-Disposition filename strips CR/LF too'), which is not in HEAD history.
suggestedFix: Provide an RFC 5987 UTF-8 filename* plus an ASCII-safe fallback: `const ascii = downloadName.replace(/[^\x20-\x7e]/g, '_').replace(/"/g, ''); const utf8 = encodeURIComponent(downloadName); res.setHeader('Content-Disposition', \`inline; filename="${ascii}"; filename*=UTF-8''${utf8}\`);`. This stops the ERR_INVALID_CHAR throw on emoji/non-Latin1 transfer names (so the attachment renders instead of failing with an opaque 500) and strips control chars as defence-in-depth.

title: Destructive dedupe runs immediately with no dry-run or confirmation guard
note: Verified as a real footgun: main() parses no argv at all and runs updateMany/update/delete unconditionally the moment `npm run imessage:dedupe-people` is invoked (package.json:20). There is no --apply/--dry-run, no preview, no confirmation. This contrasts with the repo's own convention for destructive scripts — cleanup-artifacts.ts defaults to a dry-run and only mutates under --apply (lines 171, 231-233), and db:reset:linkedin requires `--confirm RESET` (package.json:17). Two adjustments: (1) category is data-integrity/operational-safety, not 'security' — there is no auth/privilege/secret dimension; (2) severity lowered to medium because the catastrophic irreversible-loss consequence is already captured at critical in the displayName-grouping finding above; the standalone 'no safety gate' issue is real but the missing-guard aspect is the secondary half of that same bug.
suggestedFix: Parse argv for --apply and default to a dry-run that prints every planned (dup -> canonical) merge plus the threads and notes that would move; only call updateMany/update/delete when --apply is passed, mirroring cleanup-artifacts.ts.

title: Destructive displayName overwrite + inferredName wipe runs with no dry-run guard
note: Verified. Lines 41-44 overwrite displayName to the resolved name and set inferredName:null in one immediate pass, with no --apply/dry-run/preview (package.json:19). The finding's own caveat is accurate and I confirmed it: the mutation is gated by looksLikeUnresolvedHandle (name-inference.ts:108, which also returns true for blank, line 110) AND a non-null resolver hit (line 37) — and resolver.resolve('') returns null (contact-resolver.ts:145), so a blank displayName lands in the `unmatched` branch and is NOT rewritten. So this is materially safer than the dedupe script. The residual risk is real, though: a stale/reassigned/mis-keyed contacts.vcf silently rewrites the wrong person's name, and `inferredName: null` is unconditional so an operator-confirmed inferredName is discarded with no preview. Medium severity fits.
suggestedFix: Add an --apply flag defaulting to a dry-run that prints every planned `oldName -> realName` rewrite; only mutate under --apply. Avoid nulling inferredName unconditionally (or log the prior value) so an operator-confirmed name remains recoverable.

title: tccutil reset AppleEvents wipes ALL Apple-Events automation permissions machine-wide with no confirmation
note: Verified. Line 22 runs execFileAsync('tccutil', ['reset', 'AppleEvents']) unconditionally with no argument scoping and no confirmation prompt; the only argv handling is the catch wrapper (lines 27-30). `tccutil reset AppleEvents` with no bundle id revokes every app's Automation grant on the machine, not just the runner/terminal -> Messages grant. The file header (lines 9-13) explicitly acknowledges 'resets ALL Apple-Events permissions on the machine' yet ships no guard, so a user fixing one denied send wipes automation for every other app, each of which must re-approve. Real broad irreversible side effect; medium is appropriate (recoverable via re-grant, single-machine, requires deliberate invocation).
suggestedFix: Gate the reset behind an explicit confirmation (require --yes/--force or an interactive y/N) and print a clear warning that it clears Automation for ALL apps. Where the requester bundle id is discoverable, prefer the scoped form `tccutil reset AppleEvents <bundle-id>`.

title: Destructive merge runs without a transaction, leaving partial state on any mid-merge throw
note: Verified. applyLinkedInRepairPlan (lines 194-295) iterates plan.merges and, per merge, loops over sourceMessages calling prisma.message.upsert one at a time (lines 227-252, incrementing messagesRepointed), then issues prisma.thread.delete for the duplicate (lines 256-260). A grep across the whole file confirms there is no prisma.$transaction anywhere. If any single upsert or the thread.delete throws partway through (DB lock, constraint, crash), the keeper is left with only the subset of messages repointed so far and the duplicate thread may still exist (if it threw before line 256). The NDJSON report is written before apply (writeRepairReport at line 402, apply at 406) and apply records no per-action progress, so there is no audit of how far the merge got; recovery is a blind full re-run. The re-run is at least idempotent-ish (upserts keyed on threadId_platformMessageKey), but the lack of an atomic boundary on a destructive dedupe is a genuine integrity gap. Medium is appropriate.
suggestedFix: Wrap each merge's per-message repoint loop plus the duplicate prisma.thread.delete in a single prisma.$transaction(...) so a mid-merge failure rolls back atomically (duplicate intact, keeper untouched). Alternatively/additionally append per-merge completion records to the report so a partial apply is auditable and resumable.

title: headlineLine 'no profile yet' fallback is unreachable
note: Confirmed. PeopleRow.headline is `string | null` (types.ts line 70), so person.headline can be null/undefined and the first ?? can fall through. But the middle term [person.currentRole, person.currentCompany].filter(Boolean).join(' at ') always returns a string — '' when both are absent — and '' is not nullish, so '' ?? 'no profile yet' evaluates to ''. The 'no profile yet' fallback is therefore unreachable, and a contact with no headline and no role/company renders a blank subtitle line instead of the placeholder. Low severity (cosmetic empty line).
suggestedFix: Use falsy-aware fallbacks: const joined = [person.currentRole, person.currentCompany].filter(Boolean).join(' at '); const headlineLine = person.headline || joined || 'no profile yet';

title: Shared single actionError string loses which platform failed and is not auto-cleared between actions
note: Verified, with a mitigation that caps severity at low. page.tsx:36 declares a single page-level actionError; it renders at the very top of the page (lines 63-64) with no platform attribution, detached from the triggering card. It is only cleared when a later action succeeds (runAction/runActionWithFeedback call setError(null) on success), so a failure followed by no further action leaves a stale top-of-page error indefinitely — both claims are accurate. Mitigation: the high-frequency actions (Scan now line 167, Open browser line 144) already route through runActionWithFeedback, which shows an attributed error TOAST and feeds setError; only the runAction paths (Reconnect/Run selector tests/Reset session and the DegradedBanner) rely on this low-fidelity shared string. So in practice this mostly compounds the finding-1/finding-2 gaps rather than being a standalone high-severity issue.
suggestedFix: Once the runAction paths (findings 1 and 2) are moved to runActionWithFeedback, every failure already carries platform context in its toast copy. Then either drop the shared actionError banner or scope/auto-expire it and include the platform name, so a stale, un-attributed error can't linger at the top of the page.

title: Demo start buttons are not double-submit guarded — repeated clicks fire multiple /control/settings POSTs
note: Verified against commit 57594f5. start() (FullDemoProvider.tsx 267-303) has no in-flight guard — no `if (starting) return`, no ref — and the buttons never disable while it runs. disabled={selected.length === 0} (line 50) guards only empty selection, not concurrency. A fast double-click on the Sandbox button (line 71) or the Start live demo Button (line 51) therefore issues two concurrent apiPost("/runner/control/settings") calls plus two writeFullDemoState/refreshSettings sequences. Impact is genuinely low: the payload is idempotent (same presenterDemoMode/presenterReadOnly) and both resolve to presenter mode, so there is no corruption — only redundant POSTs and interleaved state writes. The cited correct pattern is real: reconnect/page.tsx handleRefreshScores starts with `if (refresh_state.kind === "running") return;` (line 77). Confirmed at low severity.
suggestedFix: Add an in-flight guard at the top of start() (early-return when a start is already pending, e.g. via a ref or the same `starting` state used for finding 1) and/or disable both buttons while pending, mirroring reconnect/page.tsx's `if (refresh_state.kind === "running") return;`. Fixing finding 1's disabled-while-starting state resolves this simultaneously.

title: events-proxy upstream fetch has no try/catch — runner-down yields an unhandled 500 instead of the intended 502
note: Verified in the working tree (identical to commit 57594f5, empty diff). The GET handler (lines 17-42) awaits fetch(targetUrl) at line 21 with no try/catch and no enclosing try/catch; there is no dashboard middleware.ts to catch it. On a runner-down condition (ECONNREFUSED/DNS/socket), fetch rejects, the handler throws, and Next returns a generic 500 — the deliberate `if (!response.body) return new Response("SSE stream unavailable", { status: 502 })` (lines 30-32) only fires for a resolved 2xx response that happens to have a null body, never for a rejected fetch. So the claim is accurate. Severity correctly low: the browser consumer (app-shell.tsx line 388 `new EventSource`, line 410 onerror "Let EventSource auto-reconnect") reacts identically to a 500 or a 502 (both → onerror → reconnect), so there is effectively NO user-facing difference; the only real cost is server-side unhandled-error log noise and not reaching the intended graceful status. Confirmed, but the practical benefit of the fix is log cleanliness / intent, not changed client behavior.
suggestedFix: Wrap the fetch in try/catch and on rejection return new Response("SSE stream unavailable", { status: 502 }) (or 503), matching the existing no-body branch, so runner-down produces a clean status instead of an unhandled 500. Purely a log-hygiene/intent improvement — the browser EventSource auto-reconnects either way.

title: saveProfileUrl reports "Failed to save profile URL" even when the save succeeded
note: Verified, though the real lines are 111-128 (the cited 128-145 is slightly off but points at the same function). In saveProfileUrl the write POST is awaited first (line 118) and succeeds; then setProfileUrlInput('') (119), then a refetch apiGet (line 120), setDetail (121), rescan (122). The single catch (lines 123-124) sets error to 'Failed to save profile URL' for ANY throw in the try. apiGet throws on any non-ok response (api.ts:37-39), so a transient blip on the line-120 refetch — after the write already persisted — is reported to the operator as a save failure. rescan() itself is fire-and-forget (line 95-109 calls runAction which swallows its own errors), so it won't poison this catch; the refetch is the realistic mis-attributed failure. The operator may then retry a save that already succeeded. Consequence is a misleading message + possible redundant save, not data loss, so low severity is right.
suggestedFix: Wrap only the write POST (line 118) in the try whose catch reports 'Failed to save profile URL'. Move the refetch+rescan after the try, or give the refetch its own catch that leaves the prior detail in place and shows a softer 'Saved, but couldn't refresh' notice, so a refetch hiccup is never reported as a save failure.

title: No success confirmation on rename/confirm — only feedback is the row silently re-fetching
note: Confirmed. On the success path (lines 63-65) the only operator-perceptible effects are the popover closing and onChanged() triggering a parent re-fetch (wired to refresh() via onPersonChanged in inbox/page.tsx:499 → selectable-thread-row.tsx/thread-row.tsx). The component imports only apiPost and never calls showToast or any TopStatus/ticker update, so a confirm/rename reads as a silent close + re-render with no positive confirmation toast or status. This is the same underlying gap as the high finding (lack of feedback wiring) rather than a separate defect, hence low severity — but the claim that there is no success confirmation is accurate. Note the cited lines 32-37 are the state-init header; the actual success path is lines 62-65.
suggestedFix: Emit a success toast on resolve — ideally fold this into the same runActionWithFeedback wrapper proposed for the high finding (success: 'Name updated'), which gives pending→success/error in one place. A standalone showToast({ kind: 'success', title: 'Name updated' }) in the success branch also closes the gap.

title: normalizePreview returns the untrimmed raw string for non-placeholder previews
note: Confirmed at preview.ts line 16: `return PLACEHOLDER_LABELS[trimmed] ?? raw;` returns the untrimmed `raw` on a placeholder miss, while the lookup uses `trimmed`. The empty-after-trim guard (line 15) only catches whitespace-only strings, so '  hello\n' falls through unmodified. Render sites use the value directly with no further trim (thread-row.tsx:25-27 renders `You: ${cleanPreview}`), so leaked whitespace would reach the UI. Impact is genuine but narrow: most preview sources are already trimmed upstream (LinkedIn previewSnippet is .replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim() at extraction, inbound message text goes through cleanMessageText in scan-queue.ts:2553, lastMessagePreview via cleanText). However send.ts:344 persists `lastMessageText: input.text` un-trimmed and thread-row-shaping.ts toInboxRow prefers lastMessageText first (line 202), giving a real path for an outbound reply's trailing whitespace/newlines to leak into the preview. Visible artifact is minor (usually invisible trailing space on a single-line truncated preview), so low severity is correct.
suggestedFix: Return the normalized value on a placeholder miss: `return PLACEHOLDER_LABELS[trimmed] ?? trimmed;` so previews are consistently whitespace-trimmed regardless of source.

title: list_hydration_timeout failure reason is unreachable (shadowed by generic 'timeout' check)
note: Confirmed. In resolveLinkedInScanFailureReason the generic branch `if (message.includes("timeouterror") || message.includes("timeout")) return "timeout"` (line 1704-1706) runs before `if (message.includes("list_hydration_timeout")) return "list_hydration_timeout"` (line 1707-1709). Because the string "list_hydration_timeout" contains the substring "timeout", any message carrying it matches the generic branch first, so the dedicated branch is dead for message-based classification. The codebase raises `new Error("list_hydration_timeout")` (line 6679, inside toStageFailure) and both catch blocks feed `error.message` into this resolver (lines 8850-8857 and 8968-8975), and the result is stored as `runCounters.stopReason = failureReason` (line 8859) and logged. So a list-hydration-timeout is mis-bucketed as generic "timeout" in telemetry. Impact is diagnostics-fidelity only (and any retry/cooldown keyed off the specific reason), no data loss — low severity is correct. The finding's cited line numbers (1717-1722, raise at 6995, callers at 9408/9526) are stale; actual lines are 1704-1709, raise at 6679, callers at 8850/8968, but the logic is exactly as described.
suggestedFix: Reorder so the specific `list_hydration_timeout` check precedes the generic `message.includes("timeout")` check, or guard the generic branch to exclude messages that match a specific *_timeout reason (e.g. test for "list_hydration_timeout" first / use a word-boundary regex).

title: scrollNoMoveStreak guard is unreachable; deep scroll stops after a single no-move instead of honoring scanStableIterations
note: Confirmed. deepScrollThreadList returns `reachedBottom: !moved` (line 3735). In collectThreadRowsWithScroll the loop increments scrollNoMoveStreak only when `!scrollOutcome.moved` (lines 4055-4059), but the very next statement `if (!scrollOutcome.didScroll || scrollOutcome.reachedBottom) break` (lines 4060-4071) fires on that same iteration because reachedBottom === !moved. So any no-move iteration both bumps the streak and breaks, meaning scrollNoMoveStreak can never accumulate past 1, and the top-of-loop stop check `if (scrollNoMoveStreak >= stableIterationsTarget)` (lines 4013-4023) is effectively dead (stableIterationsTarget = Math.max(1, scanStableIterations), line 3796). The other two stop paths (noProgressStreak line 3989, bottomRepeatStreak line 4001) DO accumulate across iterations and honor stableIterationsTarget, which highlights that the no-move path is the anomaly. Net effect: for the scroll-no-move path, collection ends on the first no-move determination rather than after N stable iterations, risking under-collection while LinkedIn is still virtualizing rows. Genuinely mitigated (not eliminated) because deepScrollThreadList performs two internal scroll attempts before reporting no-move (lines 3710-3731). Severity low (collection-tuning/under-collect risk, not corruption) is appropriate. Finding's cited line numbers (4250, 4292-4297) are stale; actual lines are 4013, 4055-4071.
suggestedFix: Decouple the immediate break from a single no-move: only break on reachedBottom once scrollNoMoveStreak >= stableIterationsTarget (mirroring the noProgress/bottomRepeat paths), or have deepScrollThreadList distinguish a definitive bottom (e.g. unchanged scrollHeight) from a transient no-move so reachedBottom isn't simply `!moved` and the streak can accumulate as intended.

title: Attachment count includes every decorative <svg>, so nearly every IG/TikTok message is mislabeled as having attachments needing manual review
note: Verified. Line 333 computes `attachmentCount = root.querySelectorAll("img, video, svg, a[download]").length` where `root` is a single message_item node, and lines 344-346 emit `[{ type: "attachment", manualReview: true, rawLabel: "N attachment(s)" }]` whenever the count is non-zero. The BetaAdapter is the INSTAGRAM/TIKTOK adapter (constructor binds this.platform; auth detection branches on INSTAGRAM/TIKTOK). instagram.json sets message_item to the loose `div[role='row'], div[role='listitem']`, and IG rows carry an avatar plus inline status/reaction/seen SVGs, so a plain text DM row will routinely yield attachmentCount > 0 and be flagged manualReview. (TikTok's `div[data-e2e='chat-message']` is tighter but reaction/status icons still render as SVGs.) The synthetic attachments are not dropped downstream: scan-queue.ts:2612/2622 persists message.attachments into attachmentsJson and the dashboard surfaces attachments[].manualReview (types.ts:226-228), so the spurious flag reaches the DB and UI. Cited line range tightened (333 + 344-346 rather than 350/368-370). Low severity is appropriate — cosmetic/noise rather than data loss.
suggestedFix: Drop `svg` (and the unscoped avatar `img`) from the selector — count only real media/file attachments scoped to the message body, e.g. `img[src]:not([alt='']), video, a[download]`, or gate on image dimensions. Decorative status/reaction/avatar icons should not register as attachments.

title: Combined message timestamp skips the future-time guard the time-only path applies, allowing a future lastMessageAt for a 'Today' header + later time-of-day
note: Verified. The time-only branch clamps the future: lines 207-213 (no date heading) build today+time and, if `candidate.getTime() > now.getTime()`, roll back to yesterday; parseLinkedInListTimestamp applies the same clamp for bare time strings (90-93, 104-107). The combined path (215-221) resolves the date heading via parseLinkedInListTimestamp then `return buildDate(dayAnchor..., hour, minute)` with no future check, and the function ends at line 221 — no trailing clamp. When the heading resolves to today ('Today' -> 73-74 gives today 00:00; or a weekday that resolves to today -> 113-122 inclusive of today gives today 00:00) and hour:minute exceeds the current wall-clock time, the returned Date is in the future. Both callers pass real wall-clock now (linkedin-adapter.ts:6274 and :7931 with new Date()) and feed combined.toISOString() into the message timestamp -> lastMessageAt/freshness, so the inflation is real. The asymmetry the finding describes genuinely exists and the function's own header comment (160-164) states it exists to prevent future-dated lastMessageAt. Severity correctly low: the realistic trigger is narrow (clock skew, or DST/timezone edges) since a real message's displayed time-of-day normally cannot exceed now on the same day.
suggestedFix: After building the combined Date at line 220, if it falls on today and its time is greater than `now`, clamp it (return `now`, or only when the heading was 'Today'/today-resolving, roll back one day) so a combined timestamp can never land in the future — consistent with the guard on the time-only branch.

title: /data/inbox returns a fabricated averageReplyTimeHours (hardcoded 4.2)
note: The code claim is exactly right: index.ts:2354 is `averageReplyTimeHours: outboundLast7DaysCount ? 4.2 : 0`, and outboundLast7DaysCount (index.ts:2254-2261) is a plain prisma.message.count of direction:'OUT' over the last 7 days — it never measures any inbound->outbound latency, so 4.2 is a hardcoded placeholder presented as an analytic. HOWEVER the finding's stated user-facing consequence ('the dashboard displays a constant 4.2h average reply time') is NOT currently true: grep across apps/dashboard shows averageReplyTimeHours appears only in lib/types.ts:50 (type decl) and is never rendered in any .tsx (inbox/page.tsx renders unreadThreads/atRiskThreads/oldestPendingInboundAt only). So this is a latent bug — any future UI or external API consumer of /data/inbox gets a fabricated number — rather than a currently-visible fabrication. Confirmed at low because the misleading code genuinely ships in the API response.
suggestedFix: Either compute the real metric (pair each inbound with the next outbound per thread over the window and average the deltas) or drop the field from the /data/inbox payload until it can be computed, instead of returning the constant 4.2. Also remove the now-dead field from lib/types.ts if not adopted.

title: Thread-mutation routes return 500 (not 404) for a non-existent threadId
note: Verified. /archive (index.ts:2934-2937), /unarchive (2975-2978), /recategorize (2856-2865), /mark-done (3870-3879) and /snooze (3933-3939) all call prisma.thread.update({ where: { id: threadId } }) with no prior existence check. asyncRoute (526-532) does `.catch(next)`, forwarding the thrown Prisma P2025 to the global handler (4097-4111), where `const statusCode = error instanceof z.ZodError ? 400 : 500` returns a generic 500 with the raw error message. grep confirms there is no P2025 / PrismaClientKnownRequestError handling anywhere. The sibling /open-loop route (2951-2958) does findUnique first and returns a clean 404, so the inconsistency is exactly as described and the client cannot distinguish a missing thread from a server fault. Low severity: these ids come from the app's own thread list, so a missing id is an edge case (stale tab / deleted thread), not a routine path.
suggestedFix: Map Prisma P2025 to 404 — either catch PrismaClientKnownRequestError with code 'P2025' in these handlers (or centrally in the global error middleware) and return 404 {error:'Thread not found'}, or pre-check with findUnique like /open-loop already does.

title: Draft save is a non-atomic find-then-create that can create duplicate Draft rows
note: Verified. POST /control/thread/:threadId/draft (index.ts:3849-3863) does findFirst then branch create/update — non-atomic. The Draft model (packages/core/prisma/schema.prisma:293-305) has only @@index([threadId]) and NO @unique on threadId, so two concurrent saves that both observe existingDraft===null (debounced autosave racing a manual Save, or a double-click) both hit create and insert two rows. The read side masks it: /data/thread reads drafts with orderBy updatedAt desc + take 1 (index.ts:2390-2393), so duplicates silently accumulate as orphan rows and make 'the draft' ambiguous. (Note: finding cites schema lines 506-517 but the model is actually at 293-305 — content matches exactly.) Low severity: SQLite serializes the file but each statement is a separate transaction, so the read-null/insert race is genuine though it requires near-simultaneous saves.
suggestedFix: Add @unique to Draft.threadId and replace the find-then-branch with prisma.draft.upsert({ where: { threadId }, update: { text }, create: { threadId, text } }) for an atomic, idempotent write.

title: /data/thread crashes (500) on a single message row with malformed rawJson/attachmentsJson
note: Verified at index.ts:2679-2680: `raw: message.rawJson ? JSON.parse(message.rawJson) : null` and `attachments: message.attachmentsJson ? JSON.parse(message.attachmentsJson) : []`, both inside pageMessages.map with no try/catch. A single corrupt value in either column throws inside the map, fails the whole /data/thread request -> global handler -> 500, blanking the entire thread view (the most common read path) instead of degrading one bubble. The fix is trivial and the pattern already exists: services/conversation-starters.ts:61 defines a reusable safeJsonParse<T>(value, fallback) helper. TWO CAVEATS that lower likelihood/severity: (1) these columns are always written via JSON.stringify (scan-queue.ts:2612-2624, send.ts:192/496), so malformation requires manual DB edits / partial writes / format drift rather than normal operation — though this is a local-first SQLite DB on the user's machine, so hand-edits are plausible; (2) the finding's claim that 'other JSON columns in the same handler are individually guarded' is FALSE — tagsJson (2646), openLoopsJson (2662), dismissedOpenLoopsJson (2666) and toneNotesJson (2668) are equally bare JSON.parse with no guard, so the per-message parse is not uniquely unprotected. The core failure mode for rawJson/attachmentsJson is nonetheless real.
suggestedFix: Wrap each per-message parse with the existing safeJsonParse helper (raw -> null, attachments -> []) so one bad row degrades a single bubble rather than 500-ing the whole thread. While there, apply the same helper to the sibling tags/openLoops/dismissedOpenLoops/toneNotes parses in this handler, which are equally unguarded.

title: getOrGenerateStarters returns null on AI outage instead of falling back to a stale cached value
note: Verified. When the cacheKey has changed (so the 181-183 cache hit is skipped) and generateConversationStarters returns null (provider unavailable / failed — it swallows errors and returns null), getOrGenerateStarters returns null at line 187 and the People-page 'Suggested openers' section renders nothing (people/page.tsx:398 gates on detail.starters.starters.length > 0). The sibling getOrGenerateSummary handles the identical case by returning the stale cached value: `if (!summary) return row.summary ?? null;` at line 162. The asymmetry is real and a transient AI outage needlessly blanks previously-good starters still on disk in row.startersJson. Low severity is right — transient, self-healing on the next successful generation, and the empty section is benign.
suggestedFix: On `!generated`, fall back to the previously cached starters when present: parse row.startersJson via safeJsonParse<ConversationStartersResult | null>(row.startersJson, null) and return it (else null), mirroring getOrGenerateSummary line 162.

title: Refinement skip/fail attempt rows hardcode model "gpt-5-nano" regardless of the configured refiner model, can collide with the unique (transcriptionId, tier, model) constraint and mislabels stored attempts
note: PARTIALLY confirmed. The mislabel half is real: the refiner model is operator-configurable via AUDIO_TRANSCRIPTION_REFINEMENT_MODEL (config.ts:593 `model: env.AUDIO_TRANSCRIPTION_REFINEMENT_MODEL?.trim() || "gpt-5-nano"`). The OK branch persists the real model (`outcome.result.model`, which is `config.model` per text-refinement-service.ts:192), while the skipped branch (line 872) and failed branch (line 881) hardcode the literal "gpt-5-nano". If the operator overrides the model, skipped/failed refinement attempt rows are stored under the wrong model id, corrupting the audit surface the schema comment (schema.prisma:496-499) explicitly exists to support. The `"unknown"` fallback at 872 is also dead — runProgressiveRefinement early-returns at line 810 when !deps.refiner. HOWEVER the P2002-collision/crash claim is REFUTED: runProgressiveRefinement is invoked from exactly one place (line 607, manual path only; the auto queue at line 348 never calls it). Each manual run that reaches refinement starts from a parent with zero pre-existing refinement attempts — force=true deletes the parent and a fresh parent row with a new cuid id is created (cascade onDelete at schema.prisma:477 removes old attempts), non-force+existing-parent short-circuits at 406-414 before refinement, and withSerial(messageId) (line 376/255) serializes all paths. So two refinement creates against the same transcriptionId never occur and the unique constraint is never violated. Net: a narrow audit-label mismatch, not a crash; severity dropped to low.
suggestedFix: Thread the configured refiner model id (config.model) into runProgressiveRefinement and use it for the `model` column in all three branches so skipped/failed rows match the OK branch. Drop the dead `deps.refiner ? ... : "unknown"` ternary. No P2002 handling is needed — the collision is unreachable.

title: defaultProcessRunner.spawn silently ignores the timeoutMs option, so the spawn-level safety net relied on by the ProcessRunner contract does not exist; only runProcess's setTimeout enforces the budget
note: Confirmed as a contract/robustness gap, not an active bug — consistent with how the finding frames it. The ProcessRunner interface advertises `options?: { timeoutMs?: number }` (lines 30-34) and runProcess calls runner.spawn(command, args, { timeoutMs: options.timeoutMs }) (line 229), but defaultProcessRunner.spawn(command, args) (line 38) takes only two parameters and never forwards timeoutMs to node's child_process.spawn, so no spawn-level `timeout`/`killSignal` is set. In practice the budget is still enforced: runProcess installs its own setTimeout that fires child.kill("SIGKILL") and resolves {kind:"timeout"} (lines 236-244), and the transcribe() consumer maps that to a failed outcome (line 130-132). So a hang is bounded today; the only exposure is a misleading contract if runProcess is later refactored to trust the runner-level timeout or a custom ProcessRunner relies on the documented option.
suggestedFix: Either honor the option in the default runner (`spawn(command, args, { stdio: [...], timeout: options?.timeoutMs, killSignal: "SIGKILL" })`) or drop `timeoutMs` from the ProcessRunner.spawn signature and rely solely on runProcess's setTimeout, so the contract matches behavior.

title: Non-zero whisper-cli exit is reported as a generic "failed"/local_whisper_command_failed even though collected stderr is discarded, losing the only diagnostic for a misconfigured model/binary
note: Confirmed. runProcess collects up to 4096 bytes of stderr (lines 246-251) and returns it on the ok result (`{ kind: "ok", exitCode, stderr }`, line 262), and the comment at lines 39-41 states stderr is collected specifically 'for short error messages on non-zero exit.' But the exitCode !== 0 branch (lines 139-144) returns a fixed `errorMessage: "local_whisper_command_failed"` and never reads result.stderr, so the captured diagnostic (e.g. a bad model path or unsupported flag) is dropped from the persisted row. Including it is safe: no dashboard code exact-matches this code (grep for `local_whisper_command_failed` in apps/dashboard returns nothing), and the failed-status path in imessage-media.tsx renders a generic hint + 'Try again' without parsing errorMessage (lines 158-160), so the stable-reason-code contract only applies to the skipped/missing_file case (lines 131-134).
suggestedFix: Append a shortened stderr slice to the message, e.g. `errorMessage: result.stderr ? \`local_whisper_command_failed: ${shortenError(result.stderr)}\` : "local_whisper_command_failed"`, so the failure reason is persisted, realizing the stated rationale for capturing stderr.

title: createReadStream passed to toFile is never explicitly closed on the upload-error path, leaking a file descriptor per failed OpenAI transcription
note: Confirmed as a narrow, very-low-severity robustness gap, consistent with the finding's own framing. createReadStream(request.filePath) is passed inline to toFile (lines 44-48) with no reference retained, and the catch at line 83 builds a failed outcome without any try/finally that calls stream.destroy(). On the happy path the stream is read to EOF and auto-closes; the unguarded window is when something throws before the stream is fully consumed (toFile throwing mid-read, or an abort), where the fd release falls to GC finalization rather than being deterministic. Real but minor: it requires repeated mid-upload failures to matter, and the descriptor is eventually reclaimed.
suggestedFix: Hold the ReadStream in a local and destroy it deterministically, e.g. `const stream = createReadStream(request.filePath); try { ... } finally { stream.destroy(); }`, so the fd is released whether the upload succeeds or throws.

title: Shrink guard rejects legitimate single-name-deletion patches and is bypassable by length-padding, because it compares total character length rather than spoken-token loss
note: Confirmed. The shrink guard rejects the refined output when `output.length / base.length < 0.88` (line 435) — raw character count — yet its own comment (433-434) frames the intent as 'patches stripped speech rather than fixing words.' Because refinement here is patch-based (verbatim from→to substring splices verified by onlyPatchedRegionsChanged at line 429), a single legitimate replacement that shortens a mis-heard phrase to a correct shorter one can trip the threshold on a short transcript: e.g. 'a maridian'(10)→'Adrian'(6) on a ~30-char note yields 26/30 = 0.867 < 0.88 and is wrongly skipped as refinement_too_short, silently discarding a correct fix. Conversely a char-padded replacement that strips words but keeps length stays under the threshold. Notably a `wordTokens()` helper already exists in this same file (line 577) and is already used by introducesDuplicateWindow (lines 563-564), so a token-based guard is readily available. The factual core (char-count guard despite a word-loss rationale; realistic over-trigger on short transcripts) holds; severity is low because it only suppresses an occasional correct patch, leaving the base transcript intact.
suggestedFix: Compute shrink over word tokens using the existing helper, e.g. `if (wordTokens(output).length / wordTokens(base).length < 0.88)`, and/or relax the threshold for short transcripts (skip the guard when base word count is below a small floor) so a single legitimate replacement isn't penalized.

title: start() skips kick() when recoverInflightOnStart rejects, leaving pre-existing PENDING jobs undrained for up to an hour
note: Verified. start() (enrichment-queue.ts:407-413) chains .then(() => kick()) onto recoverInflightOnStart(), with .catch only logging. If recoverInflightOnStart's updateMany rejects (transient SQLite lock/error at boot), the .then is skipped so kick() never fires. There is no other boot-time kick (index.ts:283 just calls enrichmentQueue.start()), and periodicTimer first fires at +1h (setInterval at 415-421). So any job left PENDING from a prior run waits until the next enqueue happens to call kick() or up to an hour for the periodic tick. Severity low: requires a recovery DB rejection at startup (uncommon) and self-heals within an hour, but the kick-on-boot guarantee is genuinely defeated by a single flaky read.
suggestedFix: Move kick into .finally so it always runs after recovery: void recoverInflightOnStart().catch((error) => console.warn(...)).finally(() => { if (!stopped) kick(); });

title: audit.log has no internal guard; fire-and-forget callers (void auditService.log) make DB-write failures completely invisible at the call site
note: Verified. log() awaits prisma.auditLog.create with no try/catch (audit.ts:17), so it rejects to the caller on any DB error. Confirmed fire-and-forget callers with no .catch: index.ts:747 and 766 (control START / END/ABORT) and 4119 (control ERROR handler). Those rejections fall through to the process-global unhandledRejection handler (index.ts:4140-4151), which only re-attempts a write to the same auditLog table (with its own .catch swallowing). Net effect when audit writes fail: the START/END control trail is dropped with zero local signal and is indistinguishable from success at the call site. Low severity: audit logging is diagnostic, not user-facing, but the gap is real and the self-referential recovery is ineffective if the table itself is the problem.
suggestedFix: Make log() self-contained so it never rejects: try { const record = await prisma.auditLog.create(...); return record.id; } catch (err) { console.warn('audit write failed', err); return ''; }. This keeps the fire-and-forget callers safe and logs the failure once via a non-DB channel.

title: Serialized write queue becomes a poisoned rejected promise after a single appendFile failure
note: Verified. Line 110 does `writeQueue = writeQueue.then(() => appendFile(prettyLogPath, ...))` and stores that chained promise back into writeQueue with no .catch, then `await writeQueue` (line 111). A single rejected appendFile (disk full, log dir removed mid-run) leaves writeQueue permanently rejected, so every later emit() chains .then() on an already-rejected promise and itself rejects (sticky, not transient). emit is the body of logLine/logStep/logLogDir, and these are awaited throughout the smoke hot path — e.g. linkedin-adapter.ts smokeUnreadIngest awaits input.logStep?.(...) at line 8167 and many `await input.logLine?.(...)` / `await logStep(...)` calls — all inside the smoke route try block (index.ts:3594-3613). So a single transient log-write error propagates out of the logging call and aborts the remainder of the smoke run (caught at index.ts:3648 as a SMOKE_FAIL) instead of being contained to logging. The mechanism is real; severity is low because this only affects the opt-in LinkedIn smoke/diagnostic path, not the user-facing inbox flows.
suggestedFix: Decouple the stored chain from the awaited result so a failed write cannot poison future log lines: `const pending = writeQueue.then(() => appendFile(prettyLogPath, `${line}\n`, "utf8")); writeQueue = pending.catch(() => undefined); await pending;`. This keeps ordering, lets the current caller see the failure if desired, and prevents one bad write from rejecting every subsequent log call.

title: prisma.$disconnect() is skipped when a mid-loop DB call throws
note: Verified literally: `await prisma.$disconnect()` is the final statement of main() (line 61), on the happy path only. If any updateMany/update/delete inside the loop rejects, control jumps to the top-level catch (lines 64-67) which logs and process.exit(1)s without disconnecting. The factual claim holds. Impact is genuinely low — process.exit tears the process (and the SQLite handle) down regardless, so this is cleanliness/best-practice rather than a leak with lasting consequence. Low severity is right.
suggestedFix: Wrap the body of main() in try/finally and call await prisma.$disconnect() in the finally so the client is closed on both the success and error paths.

title: stat() on individual run entries is unguarded against TOCTOU removal, aborting the whole cleanup
note: Verified. collectRunCandidates() readdirs a directory (lines 38, 54) then calls stat() per entry with no try/catch (line 45 for non-date first-level dirs, line 60 for run dirs); collectFlatFileCandidates does the same at line 82. The pathExists guard (lines 24-31) only wraps each root, not the children between readdir and stat. Since the runner actively writes/rotates run/screenshot/dom_dump artifacts, an enumerated entry can vanish before stat(), throwing ENOENT, which rejects the Promise.all collect step and aborts the run via the CLI catch -> process.exit(1) (lines 251-255). The mechanism is exactly as described. Severity low is right: narrow race window, the job is idempotent and re-runnable, and the default mode is a non-destructive dry-run.
suggestedFix: Wrap each per-entry stat() (lines 45, 60, 82) in try/catch and skip entries whose stat throws ENOENT (treat a vanished entry as already-cleaned) so a concurrent deletion does not abort the whole collect/cleanup run.

title: CLI entry point has no .catch — apply failures surface only as an unhandled rejection
note: Verified. The CLI guard (lines 435-440) is runRepairLinkedInThreads().finally(async () => { ...$disconnect... }) with no .catch and no explicit process.exit(1). I confirmed by grep that the only .catch/process.exit in the file is absent here, whereas the two sibling destructive scripts both have explicit handlers: reset-linkedin-inbox.ts lines 68-77 (.catch logging '[admin-reset] ...' and process.exit) and purge-automated-imessage.ts lines 79-82 (.catch logging '[purge] failed' and process.exit(1)). So if buildLinkedInRepairPlan, the report write, or the destructive applyLinkedInRepairPlan throws, the rejection is unhandled — $disconnect still runs in finally, but the failure appears only as a raw Node unhandledRejection stack with no script-prefixed log. Downgraded from medium to low: this is an observability/consistency gap, not a data-integrity defect — Node still exits non-zero on an unhandled rejection by default and the data risk is already captured by finding #2.
suggestedFix: Mirror the sibling scripts: add a .catch on the entry call that logs a clear prefixed error (e.g. console.error('[repair-linkedin-threads] failed', err)) and calls process.exit(1), keeping the existing $disconnect in finally.

title: Destructive purge has no dry-run or confirmation guard
note: Verified. main() runs straight through: it classifies automated chat.db guids, finds IMESSAGE threads whose platformThreadId is in that set (lines 47-52), and at line 62 calls prisma.thread.deleteMany unconditionally (then cascade context and orphan-Person deletion at 64-72). There is no --apply/dry-run flag, no confirmation token, and no count-then-prompt — the only early exit is the 'no automated threads found' no-op (lines 54-59). This contrasts with the gated companions: reset-linkedin-inbox.ts requires ADMIN_RESET_TOKEN + confirm 'RESET' via validateAdminResetGuards, and repair-linkedin-threads.ts is dry-run unless --apply. I also confirmed looksLikeAutomatedSender (imessage-db.ts lines 62-74): emails (contains '@') are kept, any identifier with >=7 digits is kept, only pure alphabetic/alphanumeric sender IDs or 2-6 digit short codes are flagged — so real group chats (long-digit GUIDs) and normal phone contacts are not classified automated, and the join is on chat.db guid. The classifier is therefore sound for real data, making this robustness rather than a guaranteed wrong-delete, but a single mis-tuning of the classifier would silently and irreversibly drop conversation history with no preview. Low is correct.
suggestedFix: Default to a dry-run that prints the classified threads/identifiers and counts, and require an explicit --apply (ideally plus a confirmation string) before issuing the deleteMany, consistent with repair-linkedin-threads.ts and reset-linkedin-inbox.ts.

title: RUNNER_PORT is parsed with raw Number() and has no fallback — a malformed value silently binds the runner to an ephemeral/unknown port
note: Partially confirmed. The asymmetry is real: line 276 uses raw `Number(env.RUNNER_PORT ?? 4001)` while every other numeric field uses parseIntOrDefault/parseTimeoutOrDefault (config.ts:218-232), both of which reject non-finite/<=0 and fall back to a default. I verified Number("")===0, and listen(0) binds a random ephemeral port (got 64950 in a live test) — so RUNNER_PORT="" (or whitespace coercing to 0) is a genuine SILENT misconfiguration: the runner comes up logging http://localhost:0 and the dashboard proxy (targeting 4001) cannot reach it. HOWEVER, the finding's central claim is WRONG for the non-numeric case: it asserts "Node coerces both 0 and NaN to pick a random free port" / "NaN also coerces to 0 at listen()". On this repo's Node (v20.20.0) app.listen(NaN) THROWS RangeError ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT, not an ephemeral bind. And index.ts:4178 wraps listen in a Promise with server.on('error', reject) plus a start().catch handler, so a non-numeric RUNNER_PORT produces a loud crash, not the 'healthy startup with broken client' described. So the real silent-failure surface is narrow (only empty/zero-coercing values), and it requires an operator to set RUNNER_PORT to an empty/blank value — hence low, not medium.
suggestedFix: Use the same guarded parser as the other numeric envs: `port: parseIntOrDefault(env.RUNNER_PORT, 4001)`. This makes empty/blank/non-numeric/<=0 values all fall back to 4001 instead of binding an ephemeral port (empty string) or throwing an opaque ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT (non-numeric).
